thread:
maya: opened PR to consolidate guardrail examples for Dedicated provisioning — includes flow diagrams, YAML snippets for tenant mapping, and a short rollback playbook. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1234
jordan: :eyes: will review today. Where are the autoscale policy examples? I only saw placeholders.
maya: in docs/ops/dedicated/guardrails.md — last section 'Autoscale examples' has TODOs. I added one sample but it's minimal.
alejandra: quick note: SLA wording under 'isolation' reads a bit strict for reserved pools. suggest 'best-effort latency' -> 'target latency' phrasing.
maya: good catch. want to propose exact wording? or I can patch.
alejandra: propose: "SLA target: 95th percentile latency target for reserved capacity; eviction leads to best-effort degradation". small tweak: drop 'preemption' word in public docs, say 'eviction'
sam: I can add an SDK snippet showing tenant label mapping code. snippet:```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
c = DedicatedClient()
c.provision_tenant('acme', labels={'env':'prod','team':'search'})
```
maya: perfect, add that under 'Quickstart: provision a tenant' and link to the terraform example.
jordan: found a small YAML nit: in `tenant-mapping.yaml` you use `tenant_id: null` but examples elsewhere use `tenant: ''` — pick one.
maya: leaning to `tenant:` empty string to be consistent with other docs. will normalize.
dev-bot: Reminder: docs checks failed on CI — broken link in docs/ops/dedicated/handbook.md (line 112)
maya: thanks bot. I'm on it.
alejandra: also can we add a brief 'rollback flow' section with steps: 1) set canary to 0%, 2) route to fallback model, 3) notify SRE channel. short bullets.
maya: done in latest commit; added bullet list and a tiny flowchart image placeholder.
sam: added SDK code link and a test snippet for integration tests.
jordan: LGTM aside from one nit on phrasing. :thumbsup: 
maya: merging after CI passes. will follow up with a separate PR for local runbook snippets for oncall.
alejandra: thanks — happy to help with the runbook.
